newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PNG govt mining arm to list on ASX on Nov 1.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PNG govt mining arm to list on ASX on Nov 1.

text.p: The Papua New Guinea government said on Thursday it expects its Mineral Resources Development Corp to list on the Australian Stock Exchange on November 1.

Of the 49 percent of the company to be sold, Papua New Guinea shareholders are expected to be offered 30 percent, with 20 percent going to Australian and New Zealand retail investors, and the remaining 50 percent to be taken up by institutions.
The government will retain 51 percent control of the company, to be called Orogen Minerals Ltd.

The float would raise about A$261 million for the PNG government. PNG investors would receive a 10 percent discount on the first 2,000 shares at 1.57 kina each, rising to 1.75 kina for subsequent shares. The offering to retail investors in Australia and New Zealand would be pitched at A$1.70 each for a minimum parcel of 2,000 shares while the amount to be paid by institutions for shares and global depositary receipts would be determined after the receipt of bids.
Orogen will hold the PNG government's stake in some of the world's largest gold discoveries, as well as petroleum assets, chairman David Beatty told a news conference.
Orogen's petroleum assets would consist of 15.75 percent of the Kutubu oilfield and 20.5 percent of Gobe, which begins production in 1998.
Both are operated by Chevron Corp.
The company would also have a 15.0 percent economic interest in the Porgera gold mine, a 20 percent holding in the Misima gold mine, an a 6.81 percent stake in the Lihir gold mine.
Porgera and Misima are operated by Placer Pacific Ltd, while Lihir is managed by a unit of RTZ Plc-CRA Ltd.

"Orogen Minerals will own a diverse portfolio of world-class mining and petroleum assets offering investors an exposure to one of the most prospective and resource rich regions in the world," Beatty said.

He said the company would not become an explorer in its own right until at least the year 2000, with growth to come from its current investments and a 25 year option agreement to take up the government's non-landowner rights in future mining or petroleum developments as well as the Ok Tedi and Bougainville copper projects.

The prospectus, which would form the basis of a roadshow presentation to potential institutional investors in Europe, Asia, and North America over the next five weeks, foreast net profit of 12.60 million kina (US$9.55 million) in the final four months of calendar 1996, rising to 41.58 million kina in 1997. The full-year profit forecast for 1996 was K58.47 million.

PNG investors would receive a final dividend for 1996 reprsenting a yield of 5.1 percent, or 2.95 toea per share, payable in April 1997. The 1997 dividend would also represent a yield of 5.1 percent, or 8.9 toea per share. The yield for other investors would be 5.0 percent.--Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
